findings.reason: the node would either stop as out-of-scope mid-run or smuggle the edit, and the write-path list is the fence the dispatch enforces.
findings.text: the deliverable requires "The worker prompt names the resolved command", but the worker prompt is composed in `reckon/crew/prompts.py` (`compose_prompt`, with the manifest block literal containing no suite-command slot) while §26's write paths are only `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` and the new test, so a node fenced to that scope cannot put the resolved command into the prompt at all

findings.reason: the repair (resolve at dispatch and surface it in the prompt) is unchanged; only the premise sentence needs to describe an absent command rather than an unresolved placeholder.
findings.text: §26 states "The worker-facing prompt shows no resolved form, so every armed worker sees the literal placeholder and has to substitute its own write paths by hand", but no line in `reckon/crew/prompts.py` carries `gates.suite_command` in any form (the only suite references there are the manifest's `tests`/`baseline_suite`/`after_suite` guidance lines), and no launch argv in `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` passes it either, so an armed worker sees no placeholder to substitute — the real gap is that the command is never surfaced, and a node asked to confirm the stated defect before repairing it will find no reproduction
